title: HIGH
tagline: Building a serious investing product for a generation that refuses to use serious-looking finance products.
summary: Markets, meet culture. A serious investing product that feels at home in the culture around it.
disciplines: Product Strategy · Product Design · Visual Direction · Fintech
scope: Brand, product, launch, waitlist, transactional design system

sections.heading: Finance had a type.
body: Dense screens. Serious language. Charts everywhere. Very little personality.
HIGH was built for a generation that grew up expecting something else from software: intuitive products, strong visual identities, and experiences that feel native to everyday life.
The challenge wasn't to make finance look younger.
sections.statement: It was to make a genuinely good investing product feel at home in the culture around it.

sections.heading: Markets, meet culture.
body: HIGH sits between two worlds.
The product still needs the depth of a serious broker: stocks, ETFs, IPOs, F&O, live data, charts, portfolios and trading tools.
But the experience could also speak through fashion, music, internet culture, creators, conversation and everyday Indian life. That became the central design tension:
sections.statement: Confident, not arrogant. Youthful, not childish. Simple, not dumbed down.

sections.heading: Making the market easier to enter
body: The first experience is one of the hardest.

Opening a demat account means navigating identity verification, KYC, bank details, income information, declarations, signatures and regulatory requirements. HIGH had to make that journey feel far less intimidating without hiding what was actually happening.
The onboarding experience was shaped as a sequence of clear, conversational steps, carrying the same personality as the rest of the product while respecting the seriousness of financial onboarding.

sections.heading: From a dashboard to a daily habit
body: The core product brings together market information, discovery and trading in one place.
But the ambition was bigger than simply putting more tools on a screen.

The dashboard combines market mood, portfolio context, watchlists, alerts, trending stocks, sector activity, news, events and dynamic discovery so the market can be understood at a glance. The product isn't just answering "What can I trade?" It's also answering:

sections.heading: Turning information into understanding
body: News became part of the product rather than a separate destination.
Instead of a feed of headlines, HIGH connects stories with price movement, affected stocks, sectors and the user's own watchlist.
That connection turns market news into something more useful than a scrolling feed.

sections.heading: Designing for the trader brain
body: HIGH's advanced surfaces are dense by necessity.
F&O requires option chains, open interest, volatility, positioning and expiry information. Screeners need to compress thousands of securities into useful signals.
The design challenge was to keep the information rich without making the interface feel intimidating. Hierarchy became the tool:
sections.statement: Show less first. Reveal more when needed.

sections.heading: Finance, with a little personality
body: The product doesn't treat personality as decoration. It runs through the interface itself.

Watchlists can feel playful. Market states can speak like people. Collectibles create moments of surprise. Badges turn progress into something visible. Buzz and polls bring the market conversation into the product.
The rule was simple:
sections.statement: Have fun around the money. Never be careless with it.

media.alt: The High Club coin — 999.9 fine silver

sections.heading: Designing a system, not a collection of screens
body: As the product expanded across stocks, ETFs, IPOs, F&O, SIPs, news, portfolios, alerts, discovery and community, consistency became a product problem of its own.
The experience needed shared patterns, hierarchy and visual behaviour while leaving room for each surface to have its own character.
sections.statement: That meant designing the system behind the screens, not just the screens themselves.

sections.heading: Carrying the idea beyond the app
body: HIGH was designed as a consumer brand around investing, not simply another brokerage interface.
The same thinking extended into campaigns, social content, onboarding communication, product language and brand moments.
The visual world pulls from contemporary Indian youth culture while keeping the financial product credible.
sections.statement: The brand doesn't sit outside the product. It lives inside it.

sections.heading: Building with restraint
body: The easiest way to make a finance app feel young is to make it loud. That wasn't the goal.
HIGH avoids turning every interaction into a joke or every screen into a meme. Personality appears where it adds energy, while money, risk and critical information stay clear.
The result is a product that can be playful without becoming frivolous.
sections.statement: Not finance pretending to be cool. Finance, redesigned.

sections.heading: From idea to a full product
body: The work stretched from the product's core trading experience into the wider ecosystem around it.

I worked across product direction, experience design, visual language and the systems connecting them, making decisions around hierarchy, complexity, discovery, engagement and brand expression as the product grew.
The challenge was never just making individual features work.
sections.statement: It was making the whole experience feel like HIGH.

result.heading: The result
body: HIGH is an attempt to change the relationship people have with their investing app.
Not by making markets less serious. By making the experience around them more human.
